body_markdown:
v0 by Vercel is known for generating React and Next.js components. The platform also supports full-stack development, including backend logic and integrations with external database and authentication providers. For builders seeking complete applications, alternatives offering[built-in infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) can reduce the need to assemble separate services.


This guide compares seven v0 alternatives for non-technical founders, small teams, and developers. It examines full-stack capabilities, managed infrastructure, pricing, and mobile workflows to help you choose a platform that can take your project from conversation to deployed application.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through familiar AI assistants** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports app development through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations without a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for ordinary connector operations.
- **Managed infrastructure reduces setup work** : Floot includes a[managed Postgres database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, backend endpoints, file storage, email, and hosting, reducing the need to configure separate infrastructure services.
- **Mobile publishing workflows are built in** : Floot supports[iOS and Android apps](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) from the same project, including testing builds and store submission workflows. Publishing requires the relevant developer accounts and store approval.
- **Pricing separates building from hosting** : Floot is free to start, with daily building-action limits on every plan. Pro and Power include monthly hosting allowances, while additional hosting usage is charged separately.
- **Full-stack apps without complex setup** : Floot helps non-technical founders and business owners turn ideas into working applications with user logins, saved data, and backend functionality, without manually configuring infrastructure or writing code.


## **What Makes a True Full-Stack Alternative to v0?**


v0 produces React and Next.js code, particularly for shadcn/ui components and Tailwind-styled interfaces. However, full-stack application development requires capabilities beyond frontend generation:


- **Database management** : Storing and querying application data without provisioning external services.
- **User authentication** : Handling sign-up, login, and session management for your application's users.
- **Backend logic** : Running server-side code, API endpoints, and scheduled tasks.
- **File storage** : Managing uploads, images, and static assets.
- **Deployment and hosting** : Publishing your application to a live URL with proper infrastructure.


v0 supports backend development and connects to services like Neon for databases and Clerk for authentication through Marketplace integrations, while deployment is handled directly through Vercel. For teams seeking integrated solutions with fewer external dependencies, the alternatives below offer varying degrees of built-in infrastructure.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development. Available building capabilities depend on the AI client's connector permissions.


### **Key Capabilities for Full-Stack Development**


- **MCP connector model** : Build apps through[supported AI assistants](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) using an existing AI subscription without separate Floot AI build-credit charges for ordinary connector operations.
- **Managed PostgreSQL database** : Full SQL access with browser-based table views and database export on every plan.
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus[Google and Microsoft sign-in](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) without separate OAuth app registration for those providers.
- **Serverless backend endpoints** : Run server-side code without managing infrastructure.
- **Mobile app conversion** : Package web apps into native iOS and Android shells, upload builds to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, and submit apps for store review using your developer accounts.
- **Email and push notifications** : Built-in transactional email with sent-message logs and support for web and mobile push.


### **Full-Stack Use Cases**


Floot serves non-technical founders building MVPs, small business owners creating custom internal tools, and agencies delivering client projects. The platform's all-in-one infrastructure handles appointment booking systems, real estate transaction tools, e-commerce shops, and SaaS products without requiring manual setup of core app infrastructure, although[live payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) require a paid Floot plan and a connected Stripe account.


For teams needing both web and mobile presence, Floot's mobile app conversion allows applications to share the same project rather than requiring a separate mobile codebase. The platform can send builds to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, though final store publishing requires your own developer accounts and approval from the respective stores.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free ($0/month)** : Free to start, with up to 100 build actions per day, 2 mobile app builds monthly, and a one-time $3 hosting credit.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10 monthly hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds monthly, and custom domains.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily build actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds.


Floot's[pricing model](https://floot.com/en/pricing) separates build-action limits from AI credits and usage-based hosting. Building through Claude or ChatGPT uses your existing AI subscription without a second Floot AI build-credit charge for ordinary connector operations, while image generation, optional Floot AI features, and in-app AI may consume Floot credits. Hosting beyond the included allowance uses prepaid hosting credit, with optional auto-reload. Annual billing provides two months free.


### **From AI Prompt to Published App**


Floot connects as an MCP server to existing AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor, allowing users to build through familiar interfaces. You describe your application in natural language, and the connected assistant can create project files, provision your database, generate authentication flows, and return a live preview. The workflow reduces the need to learn a separate development interface, although some publishing and account-connection steps must be completed on Floot's website.


The platform includes managed PostgreSQL, authentication with brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth, serverless backend endpoints, file storage for uploads and assets, email sending with delivery logs, and[scheduled jobs](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/jobs) for recurring tasks on published apps with a paid project owner. For teams building multiple projects, this integrated infrastructure reduces the need to assemble external services.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI app builder with built-in cloud infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Lovable Cloud infrastructure** : Database powered by Supabase, authentication, and edge functions
- **Two-way GitHub sync** : Repository connection for professional workflows
- **Visual and conversational building** : Chat-based iteration and visual editing tools
- **Pre-built integrations** : Connector library for common SaaS services


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable's two-way GitHub synchronization makes it suitable for organizations with existing Git workflows that want AI-assisted development without abandoning version control practices. The credit-based system meters AI building interactions, with additional credits available when monthly allocations are consumed.


Lovable focuses on web applications, including mobile-responsive websites and progressive web apps (PWAs). It does not provide a built-in workflow for packaging and submitting native apps to the App Store or Google Play.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable offers a Free plan with 5 daily build credits and a 30-credit monthly cap. Paid plans start with Pro ($25/month), including 100 monthly credits, custom domains, GitHub integration, and collaboration features. Business ($50/month) starts with 100 monthly credits and adds advanced organizational controls. Teams that need two-way Git integration and can work within credit-based metering may find Lovable suitable for web application projects.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new, built by StackBlitz, is a browser-based AI app builder that runs development environments using WebContainer technology.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based development** : WebContainer runs development environments in the browser, while Bolt Cloud provides integrated hosting, databases, and authentication
- **Multi-framework support** : React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular
- **Bolt Cloud** : Database and authentication services
- **Instant preview** : No local environment configuration required
- **GitHub integration** : Import, export, and sync capabilities


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new provides rapid prototyping capabilities with instant browser-based previews. The browser-based architecture means developers can start building immediately without installing dependencies or configuring local environments. The platform supports multiple JavaScript frameworks, while v0 primarily defaults to Next.js for full-stack development.


Bolt uses token-based metering, where larger projects and extensive iteration can consume tokens more quickly. It also supports mobile development workflows through Expo.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers a Free plan with 1 million tokens monthly and a 300,000 daily cap. Pro ($25/month or $18/month billed annually) provides 10 million tokens monthly with no daily cap. Teams needing instant browser-based previews and agencies producing rapid client demos may find Bolt.new suitable for application development across multiple JavaScript frameworks.


## **4. Replit**


Replit is an established coding platform that has expanded with AI Agent capabilities for assisted development.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Multi-language support** : Supports 50+ programming languages including Python, Ruby, Go, and JavaScript
- **Replit Agent** : AI-assisted coding and application generation
- **Collaborative development** : Real-time multiplayer editing
- **Instant deployment** : One-click publishing for applications
- **Education focus** : Strong presence in learning and educational contexts


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit positions itself for developers seeking broader language support beyond the JavaScript ecosystem. The platform's Agent can generate full applications for both non-technical builders and developers, while also providing code-level control when needed. The credit-based pricing for AI Agent usage scales based on project complexity.


Replit also supports mobile development workflows, including native iOS app-building and guided App Store submission capabilities. Publishing requires an Apple Developer account and standard store review.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit offers a Free plan with basic features and limited AI capabilities. Core ($20/month or $18/month billed annually) includes $20 in monthly credits, unlimited workspaces, and AI Agent access. Pro ($100/month or $90/month billed annually) includes $100 in monthly credits and greater usage allowances. Teams working across multiple programming languages or needing collaborative and educational features may find Replit suitable for diverse development projects.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app builder with entry-level pricing options, acquired by Wix in June 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-led app building** : Conversational interface for application generation
- **Database and authentication** : Built-in infrastructure services on all plans
- **Analytics integration** : Usage tracking for applications
- **Lower price point** : Entry pricing for cost-conscious teams


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 targets builders seeking lower-cost entry points for AI app development. The platform includes integrated database, backend, and authentication functionality on its Free plan, with paid plans primarily increasing capacity and adding advanced features.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 offers a Free plan with 25 monthly message credits and 100 integration credits. Starter ($16/month billed annually, or $20/month billed monthly) provides higher credit limits, unlimited apps, and in-app code editing. Builder ($40/month billed annually, or $50/month billed monthly) adds two-way GitHub sync and additional capacity. Budget-conscious teams testing AI app development within message-based credit limits may find Base44 suitable for web application projects.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual app builder that predates the current wave of AI-assisted development, offering workflow tooling and a plugin ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual development** : Drag-and-drop interface for building without code
- **AI Agent** : AI assistance for building and editing applications
- **Workflow automation** : Complex logic and business process building
- **Plugin marketplace** : Extensive ecosystem of third-party extensions
- **Database and hosting** : Integrated infrastructure for applications


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble provides full-stack capabilities through visual development alongside an AI Agent that assists with building and editing applications. The platform supports native iOS and Android apps through its mobile development workflows. The learning curve differs from conversational AI-first builders, but the platform offers established tooling for complex business applications. Bubble uses workload-based pricing that scales with application complexity and usage.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble fits teams who prefer visual development paradigms with AI assistance. The platform offers full-stack infrastructure including database and hosting, with costs that grow based on application traffic and workflow complexity. A Free plan supports development and testing, while publishing requires a paid plan. Starter costs $32/month for web, $42/month for mobile, or $59/month for web and mobile when billed annually; monthly billing costs more. Organizations building complex business applications with visual tools may find Bubble suitable for web and mobile projects.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible ChatGPT users create, preview, and publish interactive websites and lightweight applications directly from ChatGPT. It supports features such as databases, file storage, and sign-in, subject to the available runtime and account settings.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-native workflow** : Build and refine sites through natural language conversations
- **Built-in hosting and storage** : Publish interactive sites with database and file-storage capabilities
- **Sharing and access controls** : Manage site visibility, collaboration, and supported sign-in workflows
- **Connected apps** : Build tools that use visitors' connected apps where supported


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites suits interactive websites, lightweight dashboards, shared tools, and applications built within ChatGPT. Some frameworks, background services, and hosting configurations may not be supported. Floot offers a different approach for teams seeking managed Postgres infrastructure, application authentication, payments, and web-to-mobile app publishing workflows through an MCP connector.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting and storage have plan-specific limits. Floot is free to start, with separate building-action allowances and usage-based hosting. Users who want to create and publish interactive tools directly within ChatGPT may find ChatGPT Sites suitable for lightweight web projects.


## **Building Full-Stack Apps With Floot**


Floot combines an MCP workflow with managed infrastructure for people who want a working, deployed application rather than generated frontend code alone. Through its[AI connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , supported assistants can create, edit, and publish projects, depending on the client's permissions.


- **Database and authentication** : Managed PostgreSQL, SQL access, and[app user logins](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) .
- **Backend and storage** : Serverless endpoints, file uploads, and managed hosting.
- **Payments and email** :[Stripe-powered payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) , transactional email, and delivery logs.
- **Web publishing** : Live URLs, hosting, and custom domain support.
- **Mobile delivery** :[Native-shell app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android.


The connected AI assistant handles development while Floot runs the application's infrastructure. Users can work through familiar tools without separate Floot AI build-credit charges for ordinary connector operations, while build-action limits and hosting fees apply. Mobile publishing requires developer accounts and store approval. Floot participated in Y Combinator's Summer 2025 batch.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes v0 different from full-stack AI app builders?**


v0 specializes in generating React and Next.js components, particularly for shadcn/ui and Tailwind-styled interfaces. The platform supports backend development and connects to services like Neon for databases and Clerk for authentication through Marketplace integrations, while deployment is handled directly through Vercel. Full-stack alternatives like Floot include managed databases, authentication, backend endpoints, and hosting as built-in features rather than external integrations, which can streamline development for teams seeking fewer external dependencies.


### **Can existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions be used with these alternatives?**


Floot operates through an MCP connector model that lets you build using your existing AI assistant. Other platforms like Lovable, Bolt.new, and Replit provide their own AI interfaces with separate subscription or credit costs. This distinction affects total cost of ownership for teams already paying for AI assistant subscriptions, as ordinary connector operations through Floot use your existing AI subscription without a second Floot AI build-credit charge, though Floot's own build-action limits, optional AI features, and hosting charges apply separately.


### **Which v0 alternative supports mobile app development?**


Floot offers built-in mobile app packaging, while alternatives such as Bubble, Bolt.new, and Replit also provide mobile development workflows. Floot packages web applications into native iOS and Android shells with App Store and Google Play testing and submission workflows. Lovable supports mobile-responsive web apps and PWAs but does not provide built-in native app-store packaging. Store publication requires developer accounts and approval.


### **How do pricing models differ between v0 and alternatives?**


v0 has a Free plan, while its Plus plan costs $30 per user monthly. Alternatives offer various models. Floot is free to start, with Pro at $25/month and Power at $100/month, daily build-action limits, and usage-based hosting. Lovable uses credit-based metering, and Bolt.new uses token-based pricing. For teams building multiple projects, total costs depend on individual building needs, hosting usage, and any separate AI subscriptions.


### **Do users own their code when using AI app builders?**


Code ownership varies by platform. Floot states that users own their project code, data, and intellectual property on every plan, with[database export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) available on all tiers. Full project ZIP download requires a paid plan. Code portability differs by platform: some provide code export or Git integration, while proprietary visual builders may not offer downloadable source code.
